title: Kindergeld in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Kindergeld is 259 euros a month for every child** since January 2026, up from 255 in 2025. It does not depend on your income and it does not change with the number of children. The figure is set in section 66 of the Income Tax Act.

**Payment reaches back six months and no further.** Section 70 (1) pays retroactively only for the six months before the month your application arrives. Until the end of 2017 a late claim could reach back four years; that changed on 1 January 2018. **Six lost months are 1,554 euros.**
**Every month you wait, one month falls out of the window.** Apply in September and March is the oldest month you can be paid for. On 1 October, March is gone and April takes its place.

**Entitlement follows your residence title, not your passport.** German, EU, EEA and Swiss citizens qualify by living here. A settlement permit or a work-bearing permit qualifies. Study, training, au pair, voluntary-service and job-seeking permits do not, unless you are employed, on Elternzeit or drawing Book III benefits.

**The Familienkasse Berlin-Brandenburg pays around 779,336 families for 1,259,193 children** (April 2025). Counters at Charlottenstr. 87 to 90, Storkower Str. 120 and Sonnenallee 282, open Tuesday and Thursday mornings only. The online service is the faster route.

**Two tax IDs hold the whole application up:** yours and the child's. A missing Steuer-Identifikationsnummer is the most common reason a file stalls, so request a replacement before you touch the form.

**Kindergeld runs to 18 automatically,** to 21 if the child is registered as looking for work, to 25 in school, university, an Ausbildung or a recognised voluntary year, and with no age limit where a disability began before 25.

**Check what sits next to it.** Kinderzuschlag adds up to 297 euros a month per child, the Kinderfreibetrag is 9,756 euros in 2026, and Berlin adds a free Kita place, a free school ticket and, from 1 August 2026, all-day care for first-year pupils.
